morning.label: Risk-Off Tilt
morning.summary: A global bond rout deepened overnight: the 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest since 2002, France became ground zero of the selloff, and the dollar rose to an 18-month high as hedge funds piled into euro shorts. AI remains the offset - a $42B Broadcom-Anthropic chip deal, Amazon's 20-year nuclear power agreement, and a blowout Accenture quarter are lifting US futures into the open. With yields at multidecade highs, every green flag gets discounted today; jobless claims, ISM, and five Fed speeches land before and during the session.

morning.take: The tape this morning is one sentence: bonds are screaming, AI is buying the dip. The 10Y just hit its highest since 2002 and the dollar is at an 18-month high — that is real tightening, not noise, and it will cap any rally until yields crack. AI capex megadeals and an Accenture blowout keep a floor under tech, but respect the rate shock: today's upside has to be earned one ISM datapoint at a time.

morning.take: The cool PCE print flipped the tape overnight: futures are up, yields are off, and the Fed hike chatter is dying down for now. Don't mistake a relief rally for a regime change — mortgage rates just hit 7.3%, consumer confidence is at a 2014 low, and the bond rout is still grinding on underneath. The session rides on whether the soft-landing bid holds past the open; any sniff of "PCE was a fluke" and the rate pain trade reasserts itself.

The one real after-hours bright spot is Micron's blowout quarter and strong guidance, which sets up the AI/memory complex for Thursday.

evening.take: The bond market ate the good news for breakfast: a cooler PCE print should have been a green day, but the 10Y hitting a 24-year high told the tape the inflation fight isn't over. The one genuinely new signal is Micron's blowout — an 11-fold data-center revenue jump with a worsening memory crunch is about as fundamental as AI-demand evidence gets. Tomorrow is a tug-of-war between that after-hours euphoria and September's bearish close; if semis can't carry the open, the 10Y keeps running the show.

morning.take: Futures ripped overnight on Trump-Xi summit talk and a Greenland-driven rare-earth frenzy — classic pre-open euphoria. evening.summary: Monday's session was a decisive AI-led risk-on move: the Nasdaq closed at a record high (its best day since August) as chip stocks surged — AMD crossed $1T on AI demand — and falling oil prices plus retreating Treasury yields unlocked the broader rally. evening.take: Monday was the kind of session that makes you want to chase — Nasdaq record, AMD crossing $1T, META's best day in over a year. The fuel is real (falling oil, retreating yields), but this rally is running on AI euphoria while a Fed official openly campaigns for more hikes. Momentum says UP for Tuesday; the risk is that good news is getting priced in very fast.

evening.summary: Across ~175 headlines, roughly two-thirds were noise — duplicates, intraday wraps, explainers restating known conditions, and opinion pieces. The genuinely new, market-moving items were few: Buffett stepping down as Berkshire chairman, hawkish remarks from Fed Chair Warsh, fresh corporate stress (VW's outlook cut, Kremlin seizing Nestlé's Russia ops, a Turkish fund scandal), and at the single-stock level, Netflix -4.8% on a Wells Fargo target cut, Boeing plunging on a CEO warning, a Wendy's franchisee bankruptcy, and a Goldman warning on S&P 500 earnings. Offsetting pockets of strength: crypto proxies surging on the week and an Accenture–Anthropic enterprise AI deal (+5.5% after hours).

evening.take: Friday's tape was a textbook 'quiet day, bad backdrop' setup: the index barely budged, but the marginal headline was almost uniformly bearish — Buffett's exit, a hawkish Fed chair, VW's warning, a Kremlin asset grab.
